title: Benchmark launches all-origin and non-China prices for six critical minerals delivered into the US
gist: Benchmark launched paired all-origin and non-China CIF North America prices for PrNd oxide, dysprosium, terbium and yttrium oxides, and gallium and germanium metal, ahead of DFARS origin rules widening to mining/refining/separation from 1 January 2027 (gallium/germanium from 18 December 2027). The first assessment (26 November) showed origin premiums ranging from ~3% (terbium) to 60% (yttrium), with PrNd at 4% serving as the cleanest test of whether DFARS alone creates a premium.

themes.theme: DFARS origin rules and China control deadlines

insights.claim: From 1 January 2027 the US DFARS restriction on covered materials widens from where they are melted or produced to where they are mined, refined and separated, bringing inputs to NdFeB and samarium-cobalt magnets under full supply-chain scrutiny.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Defence magnet supply chains must prove non-China mining/refining/separation origin from Jan 2027 — watch demand for compliant rare earth separation capacity.

insights.claim: DFARS origin restrictions extend to gallium and germanium on 18 December 2027, roughly a year after rare earth magnet inputs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: A second compliance cliff for gallium/germanium supply in late 2027 is a dated catalyst for non-China producers.
insights.locator: Gallium and germanium follow on 18 December 2027

insights.claim: China's pause on its expanded rare earth export controls expires on 10 January and its suspension of the US export ban on gallium, germanium and antimony expires on 27 January, creating near-term supply-shock risk alongside the DFARS change.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Two January expiry dates are binary event risks for rare earth, gallium, germanium and antimony prices into the US.

insights.claim: Benchmark argues that from January 2027 the origin of a critical mineral becomes a matter of compliance and cost for US defence supply chains, not just sourcing preference.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Origin becomes a priced attribute — expect a bifurcated market with a measurable China vs non-China spread.
insights.quote: "From January, where a critical mineral comes from becomes a question of compliance and cost for US defence supply chains,"
insights.locator: From January, where a critical mineral

insights.claim: Benchmark launched two sets of CIF North America prices — all-origin and non-China-origin — for PrNd oxide, dysprosium oxide, terbium oxide, yttrium oxide, gallium metal and germanium metal, each combining contract and spot transactions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Observable origin-split price references enable contracts, price floors and potentially derivatives keyed to non-China supply.
insights.locator: Benchmark has launched two new sets

insights.claim: Before these grades, prices for these critical minerals did not distinguish Chinese from non-Chinese supply, leaving defence contractors unable to show compliant material is available at a reasonable price and leaving policymakers without an observed reference for price floors and border adjustments being negotiated with allies.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Allied price-floor and border-adjustment negotiations now have a benchmark to anchor on — relevant to non-China rare earth producers' revenue.
insights.locator: Until now, prices for these materials

insights.claim: Benchmark's non-China grade follows DFARS logic: Taiwan-origin material is treated as Chinese origin, while recycled material processed outside China counts as non-China origin.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Recycled feed processed outside China qualifies as compliant supply — a structural tailwind for ex-China rare earth/magnet recyclers.

insights.claim: In Benchmark's first assessment on 26 November, the non-China origin premium was about 3% for terbium, 4% for PrNd, 7% for germanium, 10% for dysprosium, 16% for gallium and 60% for yttrium.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Yttrium's 60% premium flags the tightest non-China market; terbium and PrNd premiums are still small, leaving room to widen.
insights.locator: In the first assessment on 26 November

insights.claim: PrNd is the only one of the six elements that China does not control for export, and its origin premium has stayed within a few percentage points of zero through 2026, making it the clearest test of whether DFARS changes alone will create a premium from January 2027.
insights.speaker: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Watch the PrNd non-China premium after 1 January 2027: a widening spread isolates the pure regulatory (DFARS) effect from export-control effects.
insights.quote: That makes it the clearest test of whether the DFARS changes alone will create a premium from January.
insights.locator: PrNd is the one element of the six
